Alex Singleton has 101 tackles through eight games, the most on the Denver Broncos by a wide margin, and he just became the third player since at least 2000 to reach 100 in his team's first eight games, according to the Broncos . On Sunday in Charlotte, his job is Chuba Hubbard, who has 540 rushing yards at 4.6 per carry for the Carolina Panthers.
 Alex Singleton's 101 tackles meet Chuba Hubbard's 540 rushing yards
 Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) rushes the ball against the Green Bay Packers in the first half at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images
 Singleton was named AFC Defensive Player of the Month on Thursday. He led the NFL with 68 tackles in October, 15 more than the next-closest player, and had 19 tackles in the Week 7 win at Arizona, the most by any player in a game this season. He also sacked Patrick Mahomes on third down in the 28-24 win over Kansas City , which led to a missed field goal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement October wasn't a fluke, either. Singleton had at least 13 tackles in four of Denver's five games that month and a tackle for loss in every one of them. The Broncos say he joined Zach Thomas and Shaquille Leonard as the only players since at least 1987 with 68 or more tackles, two sacks and five tackles for loss in a five-game span.
 Those numbers come with a catch. Linebackers pile up tackles when teams run at them, and opponents have run 228 times against Denver, 28.5 carries per game. The Broncos allow 127.9 rushing yards per game and 4.5 yards per carry, according to ESPN's team stats .
 Put the numbers together and Singleton is making 12.6 tackles per game, while Hubbard is getting 16.9 carries per game. Hubbard is averaging 77.1 rushing yards a game with five touchdowns and 32 rushing first downs, and Carolina's offense runs through him when it's working.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hubbard has only two runs of 20 yards or more, so Carolina's ground game is about volume and staying ahead of the sticks rather than big plays. That approach broke down in the 27-19 loss at Green Bay on Oct. 29, when Bryce Young was pressured on 48.9% of his dropbacks . Carolina doesn't want to put him in that spot again behind a line without right tackle Taylor Moton.
 Why the Broncos need Singleton to win early
 Oct 15, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton (49) reacts after a sack in the fourth quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images
 Denver's defense is built to rush the passer. Zach Allen has 4.5 sacks, and Malcolm Roach and Nik Bonitto have 3.5 each. None of that matters if Hubbard is gaining five yards on first down, because Carolina can stay in manageable down-and-distance and keep the rush from teeing off.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That's where Singleton's tackles become stops. If he's meeting Hubbard near the line of scrimmage, the Panthers end up in second-and-8, and the Broncos' edge rushers get the passing downs they want against a quarterback playing on a bad ankle.
 The Broncos are also playing without safety Brandon Jones, who was ruled out with a hamstring injury, according to The Gazette . Jones is Denver's second-leading tackler, and fewer bodies on the back end mean more of the run defense falls on the linebackers. Justin Strnad and Que Robinson will have to finish plays around Singleton.
 Denver has won four straight and sits atop the AFC West , with a bye waiting after Sunday. A Carolina team missing its top four cornerbacks doesn't have many ways to keep pace if its run game stalls.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Singleton's tackle total says the Broncos have been asked to stop the run a lot this season. Against Hubbard, the number that matters is how many of those tackles happen before he gets four yards. Do that a few times early, and Carolina ends up exactly where Denver's pass rush wants it.
